title: The frontend's port list shows a misspelt "Teestort", a shouted "TILBURY", a "Portsmouth  Port" with a doubled space and "Port of Sheerness" twice under the same code; DR1 shows each of those places once and spelt correctly.

finding.frontend: Four of the 78 port names a user reads are malformed (src/server/app/services/_capture/fixtures/ports-of-entry.json:256-304). "Teesport" is spelt "Teestort". "Tilbury" is rendered "TILBURY" in capitals while two neighbouring entries read "Tilbury Port" and "Tilbury 2 Ro-Ro Terminal". "Portsmouth  Port" carries two spaces between the words. And Sheerness appears twice, both labelled "Port of Sheerness", under the codes "GBSHS" and "GB SHS" — the same code with and without its space, so the user is asked to choose between two options that are indistinguishable on screen.
finding.prototype: DR1's port list carries "Teesport - GBTEE", "Tilbury - GBTIL" and "Sheerness - GBSHS", each spelt in sentence case and each appearing once (app/views/arrival-details.html:67).
finding.difference: Correct the four labels in the port reference data: spell Teesport, put Tilbury in sentence case, remove the doubled space in Portsmouth Port, and collapse the two Sheerness rows onto the single correct code. This is a data fix rather than a page change. It is worth doing whichever way the wider question about the port list is settled, though if that question replaces the dataset outright it goes with it.
finding.falsifiedBy: Finding "Teestort", "TILBURY" or a second "Port of Sheerness" in DR1's port list, which would make these shared defects rather than frontend ones — DR1's list contains none of the three.

relatedTo.why: both change the same port dataset
